Mini donuts on the bleachers with your nephew sounds like the right way to do a fair.
On the drive home we talked about renting a canoe at Alouette Lake before it gets too cold, the way my uncle used to take me.
A canoe trip the way your uncle did it carries a lot with it.
What did I tell you about the fall fair?
Actually, all I want to know is who I went with.
You went with Theo — your nephew. You took him to the fall fair, and you two shared a paper cone of mini donuts on the bleachers by the tractor pull.
And what was it we said about the canoe?
You talked about renting a canoe at Alouette Lake before it gets too cold — that came up on the drive home. And you said it was something your uncle used to do with you.
Never mind that. Is it too late in the year to plan the lake trip?

I don't know that lake's rental season — that's not something I can check. My honest read: mid-October in BC, the water's already cold, and a lot of rental places around here wrap up around Thanksgiving, which just passed. So it might be tight, but I'd be guessing about Alouette specifically.

No advice unless they ask for it; no coaching, planning, or nudging them toward change; no caretaking instructions like telling them to rest or drink water.
